description: Dimensional regression tests for the Manhattan Bridge control skeleton. Expected values are independent restatements of GEOMETRY-CONTROL.md and of the HO table in SCALE-HO.md, so a silent change to either document fails here. Run with: python scripts/validate_dimensions.py

modes.assert: must pass; a failure fails the suite
modes.report_only: deviation is recorded, never fails the suite; used where the prototype value has an unresolved open question

tests.title: Suspended length identity
tests.rationale: Internal consistency of the Tier A control set.

tests.title: Main span in meters
Side span in meters
Total bridge and approaches in meters
Handoff tower height above MHW is still recorded
tests.rationale: Retained for traceability but no longer drives geometry; CTL-018 does. See CONF-005.

tests.title: Center clearance above MHW in meters
Cable saddle elevation control
tests.rationale: 322.5 ft, stated directly by SRC-015. Replaced the 330 ft figure previously transmitted through SRC-012, see CONF-005.

tests.title: Deck overall width
tests.rationale: 120 ft, sourced from the 1909 cross-section. Was a placeholder at Milestone 1.

tests.title: Deck width closes against the truss and footwalk layout
tests.rationale: Independent cross-source closure check. 2 x (48 ft outer truss centerline + 10 ft footwalk) = 116 ft against the sourced 120 ft deck, leaving a 4 ft residual, about 2 ft per side. That residual is the outboard edge allowance: half the outer truss width plus fascia and railing. Recorded rather than asserted because no source states the edge detail. See OQ-014.

tests.title: Manhattan tower station
Brooklyn tower station
Manhattan anchorage cable point station
Brooklyn anchorage cable point station
Origin is the main span midpoint
Approach ends are asymmetric, per the sourced ratio
tests.rationale: A non-zero sum proves the 0.5143 sourced split replaced the Milestone 1 symmetric placeholder. Manhattan is the longer approach, so the sum is negative: approach_total x (1 - 2 x 0.514344) = -34.41 m.

tests.title: Cable saddle elevation
Navigation clearance elevation
Truss top chord equals clearance plus the ACTIVE truss depth
tests.rationale: Guards against a silent switch to the 26 ft variant, CONF-002.

tests.title: Tower foundation descends below the datum
tests.rationale: 92 ft below MHW. New at Milestone 2; retires OQ-003.

tests.title: Derived main span sag
tests.rationale: 160.5 ft. Saddle elevation minus truss top chord minus the minimum suspender length. Moved from 168 ft at Milestone 2 when SRC-015 supplied a directly sourced 322.5 ft saddle.

tests.title: Derived sag ratio is structurally plausible
tests.rationale: Suspension bridge main span sag ratios lie between about 1/7 and 1/12. A derived value outside that band would indicate a control error.

tests.title: Cable low point clears the truss top chord
tests.rationale: Equals the minimum suspender length. A negative result would put the cable through the deck.

tests.title: Vertical build-up: SRC-016 elevations against the SRC-015 summary height
tests.rationale: The model follows SRC-016's explicit elevations: cutting edge at -92 ft, capstone at +23 ft, so 115 ft overall. SRC-015 independently summarises 123 ft foundation-to-capstone. The recorded deviation is that 8 ft (2.44 m) disagreement between two directly examined period primaries, tracked as OQ-016. This test exists to keep the discrepancy visible until SRC-004 settles it.

tests.title: Caisson top elevation
tests.rationale: 44.5 ft below MHW: cutting edge 92 ft down plus the 47.5 ft caisson height stated by SRC-016.

tests.title: Masonry pier footing is seated between the caisson top and the datum
tests.rationale: SRC-016 places the footing seat 33 ft below high water and the caisson top 44.5 ft below, an 11.5 ft interval. A negative result would mean the pier was seated inside the caisson.

tests.title: Modelled tower spacing equals the main span
Modelled anchorage spacing equals the suspended length
Model longitudinal extent equals the total bridge and approaches length
Model vertical extent spans caisson underside to the top of the cable at the saddle
tests.rationale: 92 ft below MHW plus 322.5 ft to the saddle plus half the 21.2 in cable diameter, because the cable is drawn as a solid tube whose centreline sits at the saddle elevation.

tests.title: Model transverse extent equals the anchorage width
tests.rationale: 182 ft. The anchorages are the widest element, intentionally wider than the 120 ft deck.

tests.title: Deck centerline control curve spans the full modelled length
Single main cable developed length against CTL-012
tests.rationale: CTL-012 is the full per-cable length including the run embedded in both anchorages, which the skeleton does not model. The expected residual is roughly 200 ft (about 61 m) of anchorage-embedded cable, consistent with the 110 ft eyebars in SRC-012.

tests.title: Derived suspender panel pitch
tests.rationale: 18.608 ft, the unique integer solution reproducing 157 panel points per cable. Replaces the Milestone 1 arbitrary 30 ft pitch.

tests.title: HO total bridge and approaches length
HO lower-level abutment to abutment
HO upper roadway portal to portal
HO anchorage to anchorage suspended length
HO main span
HO side span
HO handoff tower height above MHW
HO center clearance above MHW
HO roadway width
HO stiffening truss depth, ASCE
HO stiffening truss depth, alternate reference
HO cable length
HO main cable diameter, ASCE
HO main cable diameter, HAER
HO deck overall width
HO suspender panel pitch is above resin print resolution
tests.rationale: 65.1 mm at HO. Recorded here so SCALE-HO.md consumers can see the physical panel pitch.

tests.title: Every part carries the required metadata fields
part_id values are unique and lowercase snake_case
Confidence grades are A, B, C or D
source_basis uses only the registered vocabulary
Weakest-link rule: no part is graded better than the worst control it consumes
Every confidence D part names an open question
Milestone 4 part coverage
Every taxonomy system required by Milestone 1 is populated
Grades of representative parts are pinned
tests.rationale: Replaces the Milestone 2 blanket ceiling on solid geometry, whose premise no longer holds: the tower caissons and piers are box envelopes whose every dimension comes from directly examined period primaries (SRC-015 and SRC-016), so grade A is correct for them. Pinning representative grades across all four bands is a stronger guard than a ceiling.

tests.title: Placeholder control census
tests.rationale: Tracks progress as sources retire placeholders. Milestone 1 closed with 19; Milestone 2 closed with 7.

tests.title: Placeholder count has not regressed since Milestone 2
tests.rationale: A ratchet. Adding a placeholder without retiring another fails the suite; retiring one requires updating this expectation downward. Raised 7 -> 10 at Milestone 6 for CTL-108, CTL-109 and CTL-110, the approach viaduct's bent spacing, bent width and girder depth. This is a deliberate, argued increase, not a relaxation: the approaches were previously drawn as a single flat slab, which concealed the fact that the structural form of 437 m of lower level and 483 m of upper roadway per side was entirely unknown. Modelling that structure makes three specific unknowns visible and countable where before there were none, which is the direction this ratchet is meant to encourage. The extent those placeholders are applied over is grade A (CTL-002, CTL-003). See OQ-020.

tests.title: The lower level reaches its sourced abutment station
tests.rationale: CTL-002 puts the lower level's abutments 5790 ft apart, grade A, so the lower deck must reach +/-882.4 m. Before Milestone 6 all deck geometry stopped at the anchorage face at +/-445 m, silently contradicting a grade-A control. This test exists so that cannot recur.

tests.title: The upper roadway reaches its sourced portal station
tests.rationale: CTL-003 puts the upper roadway's portals 6090 ft apart, grade A. The upper roadway therefore runs 300 ft further out than the lower level's abutments, and the model must show that difference rather than ending both decks together.

tests.title: Every part carries a material assignment from the control document
tests.rationale: A part with no material rule means the control document does not say how it should look, and the renderer would be choosing. Section 7 has no default rule for exactly this reason, so this test guards the section 7 table against drifting behind the part list.

tests.title: No element of this bridge claims to be measured
tests.rationale: MEASURED means the geometry derives from an instrument reading of the actual structure. Nothing here qualifies, and SRC-018 independently reaches the same conclusion for both East River subway bridges. Report-only rather than assert, because the day photogrammetry or survey lands this number should rise, and the suite should announce that rather than block it.

tests.title: Every part carries a derived geometry provenance
tests.rationale: Geometry provenance is rendered as line style, so a part without one would be drawn with no uncertainty signal at all — the silent failure the two-field schema exists to prevent.

tests.title: Assumed geometry is confined to elements no source mentions
tests.rationale: Only the two approach bent groups are ASSUMED: no registered source mentions a bent on either approach. Everything else expresses at least one sourced control, which makes it INFERRED rather than ASSUMED. A rise here means geometry was added that nothing documents, which is the one thing this project must not do quietly.

tests.title: The lower level is continuous through the anchorages
tests.rationale: CTL-002 describes the lower level as running abutment to abutment, so it cannot break. Until Milestone 7 the approach decks and all four tracks started at the anchorage's outboard face rather than its cable point, leaving a 72.2 m hole per side — the anchorage's own length — where the roadway and rails simply stopped and resumed. The roadways pass through the anchorage, which is why CTL-052 registers a 46 ft thoroughfare arch through each one. This measures the largest longitudinal gap in the lower-level chain and asserts it is closed.

tests.title: The presentation layer has not moved any geometry
tests.rationale: CONFIDENCE-MODEL.md section 7 draws a hard line: a presentation change may alter how a surface is lit, shaded or coloured, and may never move a vertex. That claim is only worth making if it is checked. This reports a digest over every emitted vertex, so a commit whose stated purpose is visual but which also shifts geometry shows up as a changed fingerprint in the validation report. Report-only, because legitimate geometry work changes it on purpose; the point is that the change is never silent.
